# morse2ascii

**Decodes Morse out of a recorded WAV file**

- **Version recorded:** 0.2.1
- **Categories:** `cw`, `listening`
- **Upstream:** <https://aluigi.altervista.org/mytoolz.htm>

## What it does

Takes a PCM WAV recording containing Morse and prints the text. It works on a file rather than on a live sound card, and it is told the tone frequency and rough speed rather than guessing them.

## Why you would want it

Offline decoding is a different job from live decoding, and it is the one that comes up when you have a recording of something you could not copy at the time — a beacon, a fragment from an SDR capture, an audio file someone sent you. Being able to re-run it with different parameters until the text falls out is exactly what a live decoder cannot do.

## Before it will work

A WAV file in PCM format. Anything else — MP3, Ogg, FLAC, or a WAV with a compressed codec inside it — has to be converted first, with sox or ffmpeg.

## How it installs

- apt: `morse2ascii`

## Known problems

It expects to be told the tone frequency and will produce confident nonsense if that is wrong, which is the usual first result. Machine-sent Morse decodes well; hand-sent Morse with irregular spacing often does not, and no parameter fixes that. For live decoding from a receiver, use xdemorse or fldigi instead.
